name: STM32F030F4P6TR
title: STM32F030x4/x6/x8/xC value-line Cortex-M0 microcontrollers, 16 to 256 KB Flash, 2.4 V to 3.6 V
summary: A 48 MHz Arm Cortex-M0 microcontroller family with 16 to 256 KB of Flash and 4 to 32 KB of parity-checked SRAM, running from 2.4 V to 3.6 V. It brings a 12-bit 1 µs ADC, a calendar RTC, eleven timers, 5-channel DMA and up to two I2C, two SPI and six USART ports, in TSSOP20, LQFP32, LQFP48 and LQFP64. STM32F030F4P6TR is the 16 KB TSSOP20 part on tape and reel.
key_figures: 16 KB / 4 KB (F4); up to 256 KB / 32 KB
VDD 2.4 V to 3.6 V; VDDA VDD to 3.6 V
22.0 mA typ at 48 MHz, 3.6 V, all peripherals on
2 µA typ (IDD, LSI and IWDG on)
12-bit, 1.0 µs, 9 external channels on the F4

notes: (1) No TIM15. (2) No TIM7. (3) No SPI2. (4) No I2C2. (5) No USART2 to USART6. (6) No USART3 to USART6.
Family references: STM32F030x4 = F4; x6 = C6, K6; x8 = C8, R8; xC = CC, RC.
A TR suffix (STM32F030F4P6TR) is tape and reel.
All parts: 48 MHz maximum CPU clock, 2.4 V to 3.6 V, junction -40 °C to 105 °C.

operation.text: A family of Cortex-M0 microcontrollers running at up to 48 MHz from one 2.4 V to 3.6 V supply, with 16 to 256 KB of Flash and 4 to 32 KB of SRAM. All carry one 12-bit ADC, an advanced-control PWM timer and up to seven 16-bit general timers, plus up to two I2C, two SPI and six USART ports. Packages run from TSSOP20 to LQFP64; ambient range -40 °C to +85 °C.

Control and user interfaces, handheld devices, audio/video receivers, digital TV, PC peripherals, games, GPS, industrial equipment, PLCs, inverters, printers, scanners, alarms, video intercoms and HVAC.

5-channel DMA; CRC unit; calendar RTC whose alarm and periodic timer wake the chip from Stop or Standby; 11 timers; up to 55 fast I/Os, all usable as external interrupt sources and up to 55 of them 5 V tolerant; SWD debug; ECOPACK 2 packages. ADC: 1.0 µs, up to 16 external channels, 0 to 3.6 V range, separate 2.4 V to 3.6 V analog supply.

SRAM is read and written at CPU speed with no wait states and carries parity checking that raises an exception. Flash holds code and data; a separate option-byte area sets write protection in 4 KB blocks and read protection. Read protection level 0 is off; level 1 blocks Flash reads and writes while a debugger is attached or after booting from RAM; level 2 also switches off the SWD port and the boot-from-RAM choice.

At reset the BOOT0 pin and a boot option bit pick one of three: user Flash, system memory, or embedded SRAM. The system memory holds a boot loader that reprograms Flash over a USART on PA14/PA15 or PA9/PA10. System memory starts at 0x1FFF EC00 on the x4, x6 and x8, and at 0x1FFF D800 on the xC.
Computes a CRC with a programmable polynomial and size; one use is checking Flash integrity at run time against a signature computed at link time (EN/IEC 60335-1).
VDD (2.4 V to 3.6 V) powers the I/Os and the internal regulator. VDDA (VDD to 3.6 V) powers the ADC, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL; it must be at least VDD at all times and come up first.

POR and PDR are always on and keep the chip in reset below VPOR/PDR (about 2 V), so no outside reset part is needed. POR watches VDD only; PDR watches VDD and VDDA. The VDDA watch can be switched off by an option bit to save current when the design guarantees VDDA ≥ VDD.

Always on after reset. Main mode serves Run; a low-power mode can be used in Stop. In Standby the regulator is off and its output floats: the core logic loses power and register and SRAM contents are lost.

Sleep stops only the CPU; peripherals run on and any interrupt or event wakes it. Stop halts every clock in the 1.8 V domain and switches off the PLL, HSI and HSE while SRAM and registers are kept; the regulator may stay in normal or low-power mode, and any EXTI line (the 16 external lines or the RTC) wakes it. Standby switches off the regulator and with it the whole 1.8 V domain, PLL, HSI and HSE; only the RTC domain and Standby circuitry keep their state. Standby ends on an NRST reset, an IWDG reset, a rising edge on a WKUP pin, or an RTC event. RTC, IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.

Wakeup times run from the event to the first user instruction after a WFE. After a WFI add 16 CPU cycles of interrupt latency. Sleep keeps the SYSCLK source; Stop and Standby wake on the 8 MHz HSI. Sleep and Stop were woken by an EXTI line in event mode, Standby by WKUP1 (PA0).

The 8 MHz internal RC is the CPU clock out of reset. A 4 to 32 MHz external clock can be selected; it is watched, and if it fails the system falls back to the internal RC, with an optional interrupt. The PLL can multiply the internal RC (x6 option) or the external clock. Prescalers set the AHB and APB clocks, both at most 48 MHz. A 40 kHz internal RC and a 32 kHz oscillator serve the RTC and IWDG; a 14 MHz RC (HSI14) is dedicated to the ADC.

Each pin is set in software as an output (push-pull or open-drain), an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down) or an alternate function; most share digital or analog functions. The configuration can be locked by a set sequence against stray writes.

Five channels moving data between memory and peripherals in any direction, including memory to memory, with circular buffers, hardware requests per channel plus software triggering, and independent source and destination sizes. Serves SPI, I2C, USART, ADC and every timer except TIM14.

The NVIC takes up to 32 maskable channels (beyond the 16 Cortex-M0 lines) at 4 priority levels, with tail-chaining, late-arrival handling and automatic state saving. The EXTI has 32 edge detectors, each set for rising, falling or both edges and masked separately, and catches pulses narrower than one internal clock period. Up to 55 GPIOs map onto its 16 external lines.

12-bit, up to 16 external channels plus two internal (temperature sensor on ADC_IN16, VREFINT on ADC_IN17), single-shot or scan conversion, DMA capable. An analog watchdog flags conversions outside programmed limits on one, several or all channels. A calibration after every power-up is advised.

Gives a voltage linear in temperature. Its offset varies part to part, so uncalibrated it suits only change detection; each part's reading at 30 °C and VDDA = 3.3 V is stored in system memory (TS_CAL1) for calibration.
A bandgap reference VREFINT on ADC_IN17; each part's value is measured in production at 30 °C and VDDA = 3.3 V and stored as VREFINT_CAL.

Advanced-control 16-bit timer: a three-phase PWM generator over six channels with complementary outputs and programmable dead time, or a general timer with four channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM and one-pulse output. Full 0-100 % modulation. Links to other timers for synchronisation; freezes in debug.

16-bit up/down counter with a 16-bit prescaler and four channels (capture, compare, PWM, one-pulse); handles quadrature encoders and one to three Hall sensors; DMA capable; links with TIM1; freezes in debug.

16-bit up counters with 16-bit prescalers. TIM14 has one channel; TIM15 two; TIM16 and TIM17 one each. TIM15, TIM16 and TIM17 each add a complementary output with dead-time insertion and a DMA request of their own, can run together, and TIM15 also links with TIM1. All freeze in debug. TIM15 exists on the x8 and xC only.
Basic 16-bit time bases. TIM6 on the x8 and xC, TIM7 on the xC only.

12-bit down counter with an 8-bit prescaler and a refresh window, clocked by the 40 kHz internal RC so it runs in Stop and Standby. Resets the chip or serves as a free-running timeout; started by hardware or software through the option bytes; freezes in debug.
7-bit down counter clocked from PCLK, with an early-warning interrupt; resets the chip on a fault; freezes in debug.
24-bit auto-reloading down counter that interrupts at zero, clocked from HCLK or HCLK/8; meant for an RTOS tick.

BCD calendar with sub-seconds to year, 12- or 24-hour format and month-length and leap-year correction. Alarm and periodic wakeup from Stop and Standby; shifting by 1 to 32767 clock pulses to sync with a master clock; digital calibration in 1 ppm steps; two tamper pins with filtering and a timestamp input, both able to wake the chip; a 50 or 60 Hz reference input for better accuracy. Clocked from a 32.768 kHz crystal, a resonator or oscillator, the 40 kHz internal RC, or HSE/32.

Up to two interfaces, multimaster or slave, Standard (100 kbit/s) and Fast (400 kbit/s); I2C1 also Fast Mode Plus (1 Mbit/s) with 20 mA drive and SMBus 2.0 / PMBus 1.1 support (ARP, host notify, PEC, timeouts, ALERT). 7- and 10-bit addressing, two slave addresses one with a mask, analog and digital noise filters, DMA. I2C2 is on the x8 and xC only.

Timing meets the I2C-bus specification rev. 03 for Sm, Fm and Fm+ when the peripheral is set up correctly. The SDA and SCL pins are not true open-drain: in open-drain mode the PMOS to VDDIOx is off but still there. Only FTf pins meet the Fm+ low-level sink current. Every SDA and SCL pin has an analog filter.
Up to six, up to 6 Mbit/s, all DMA capable; features per instance in the USART implementation table.

Up to two, master or slave, up to 18 Mbit/s, full or half duplex, frames of 4 to 16 bits, 3-bit prescaler for 8 master clock rates. SPI1 and SPI2 have the same features; SPI2 is absent on the x4 and x6.
ARM SW-DP serial wire debug on PA13 (SWDIO) and PA14 (SWCLK).

Every supply pair (VDD/VSS, VDDA/VSSA) takes ceramic decoupling as in the supply circuit, placed at the pins or right under them on the far side of the board. The 10 nF on VDDA is a good-quality ceramic closest to the chip.

Voltages are to VSS. Min and max hold over the worst ambient, supply and frequency, production-tested at 25 °C and TAmax; values marked as characterization, simulation or design are not tested and characterization limits are mean ±3σ. Typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = VDDA = 3.3 V and are not tested.

Supply currents are measured running CoreMark-equivalent code with all I/Os in analog input mode and peripherals off unless stated, Flash at 0 wait states without prefetch up to 24 MHz and 1 wait state with prefetch above, and fPCLK = fHCLK. For the typical table the PLL serves frequencies above 8 MHz and the AHB prescaler is 2, 4, 8 and 16 for 4 MHz, 2 MHz, 1 MHz and 500 kHz.

An input with pull-up held low draws current through the pull-up; output loads add their own. An input sitting at a mid-level voltage draws current in its Schmitt trigger; analog mode avoids this, and ADC inputs belong in analog mode. A floating input can drift to a mid level or toggle from noise, so unused pins are set to analog mode or held at a definite level by a pull or by output mode.

A GPIO sinks or sources up to ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH. The total sourced by all I/Os plus the chip's own VDD current stays within ΣIVDD; the total sunk plus its VSS current within ΣIVSS.
These three run from a power switch that sinks about 3 mA, so as outputs they are limited to 2 MHz into 30 pF and may not source current.
In bypass mode the HSE (or LSE) oscillator is off and OSC_IN (or OSC32_IN) is a standard input; the clock must meet the I/O characteristics.

A 4 to 32 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator. CL1 and CL2 are high-quality ceramic, 5 pF to 20 pF, normally equal, sized so their series value plus pin and board capacitance (about 10 pF) matches the crystal's specified load. Resonator and caps go as close to the pins as possible. Crystal selection is covered in application note AN2867.
A 32.768 kHz crystal with a load cap per pin and four drive levels; no resistor between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT is allowed. Place it close to the pins.

CMOS input with a permanent pull-up RPU. Pulses under 100 ns are filtered; pulses over 300 ns (VDD above 2.7 V) or 500 ns (2.4 V and up) are taken. A 0.1 µF to ground guards against parasitic resets; an outside driver must take the pin below VIL(NRST) max.

Cparasitic, the board plus pad capacitance (about 7 pF), lowers accuracy as it grows; a lower fADC recovers it. Negative injection into one analog input corrupts conversions on others; a Schottky diode to ground on such pins is advised.

EMS was tested with the chip toggling two LEDs while ESD (IEC 61000-4-2) was applied to the pins and fast bursts (IEC 61000-4-4) through 100 pF onto VDD and VSS; a reset restores operation. Software should cope with a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers; forcing NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s reproduces most such faults (application note AN1015). Emission was measured to IEC 61967-2.
TJ never exceeds the operating limit. PD is the internal power IDD × VDD plus the power dropped in the output stages.
Parts marked ES or E, or shipped with an engineering-sample letter, are not qualified for production.
